title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate access control policy and procedures that address purpose scope roles responsibilities management commitment coordination and compliance.
discussion: Access control policy and procedures address the controls in the AC family.
enhancements: AC-01(01): Policy reviewed and updated periodically.

title: Account Management
control_text: Define and document account types; assign account managers; require prerequisites for group membership; specify authorized users and access authorizations; require approvals for account creation; monitor account use.
discussion: Account management includes identification of account types and establishment of conditions for group and role membership.
enhancements: AC-02(01)-AC-02(13): Various enhancements for automated management and monitoring.

title: Access Enforcement
control_text: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
discussion: Access control policies control access between active entities or subjects and passive entities or objects.
enhancements: AC-03(02)-AC-03(15): Dual authorization; mandatory and discretionary access control; RBAC.

title: Information Flow Enforcement
control_text: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems.
discussion: Information flow control regulates where information can travel within and between systems.
enhancements: AC-04(01)-AC-04(08): Object security attributes; processing domains; dynamic flow control.

title: Separation of Duties
control_text: Identify and document duties requiring separation; define system access authorizations to support separation of duties.
discussion: Separation of duties addresses potential for abuse of authorized privileges and helps reduce risk of malevolent activity.
enhancements: AC-05(01): Automated mechanisms for separation of duties.

title: Least Privilege
control_text: Employ the principle of least privilege allowing only authorized accesses necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.
discussion: Organizations employ least privilege for specific duties and systems.
enhancements: AC-06(01)-AC-06(10): Authorize access to security functions; non-privileged access; review of privileges.

title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
control_text: Enforce a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a defined time period; automatically lock account or delay next logon when maximum attempts exceeded.
discussion: The need to limit unsuccessful logon attempts applies regardless of whether logon occurs via local or network connection.
enhancements: AC-07(01)-AC-07(04): Automatic account lock; purge mobile device.

title: System Use Notification
control_text: Display system use notification message before granting access; retain notification until users acknowledge conditions.
discussion: System use notifications can be implemented using messages or warning banners displayed before login.

title: Device Lock
control_text: Prevent further access by initiating device lock after defined inactivity period; retain lock until user reestablishes access.
discussion: Device locks are temporary actions taken to prevent logical access when users move away from systems.

title: Session Termination
control_text: Automatically terminate a user session after defined conditions or trigger events.
discussion: Session termination addresses termination of user-initiated logical sessions for local network and remote access.

title: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
control_text: Identify user actions that can be performed without identification or authentication; document and provide supporting rationale.
discussion: Specific user actions may be permitted without identification or authentication if organizations determine it is not required.

title: Remote Access
control_text: Establish and document usage restrictions configuration requirements and implementation guidance for remote access; authorize each type prior to allowing connections.
discussion: Remote access is access to organizational systems through external networks such as the Internet.
enhancements: AC-17(01)-AC-17(04): Monitoring; encryption; managed access control points; privileged commands.

title: Wireless Access
control_text: Establish configuration requirements connection requirements and implementation guidance for wireless access; authorize each type prior to allowing connections.
discussion: Wireless technologies include microwave packet radio 802.11x and Bluetooth.
enhancements: AC-18(01)-AC-18(05): Authentication and encryption; disable wireless; restrict configurations.

title: Access Control for Mobile Devices
control_text: Establish configuration requirements connection requirements and implementation guidance for mobile devices; authorize connection to organizational systems.
discussion: A mobile device is a computing device with small form factor designed to operate without physical connection.
enhancements: AC-19(05): Full device or container-based encryption.

title: Use of External Systems
control_text: Establish terms and conditions or identify controls for external systems; allow authorized individuals to access system from external systems or restrict/prohibit use.
discussion: External systems are used by but not part of organizational systems.
enhancements: AC-20(01)-AC-20(02): Limits on authorized use; portable storage devices.

title: Information Sharing
control_text: Enable authorized users to determine whether access authorizations match information access restrictions; employ mechanisms to assist in sharing decisions.
discussion: Information sharing applies to information that may be restricted based on formal or administrative determination.

title: Publicly Accessible Content
control_text: Designate individuals authorized to make information publicly accessible; train authorized individuals; review proposed content before posting; review content periodically.
discussion: Organizations ensure publicly accessible information does not contain nonpublic information.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate awareness and training policy and procedures.
discussion: Awareness and training policy and procedures address the controls in the AT family.

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
control_text: Provide security and privacy literacy training to system users as part of initial training and periodically thereafter; employ techniques to increase awareness.
discussion: Organizations provide basic and advanced levels of literacy training to system users.
enhancements: AT-02(02)-AT-02(06): Insider threat; social engineering; suspicious communications; APT.

title: Role-Based Training
control_text: Provide role-based security and privacy training before authorizing access and periodically thereafter; update training content periodically.
discussion: Organizations determine training content based on assigned roles and responsibilities.

title: Training Records
control_text: Document and monitor training activities including awareness and role-based training; retain individual training records.
discussion: Documentation for specialized training may be maintained by individual supervisors.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate audit and accountability policy and procedures.
discussion: Audit and accountability policy and procedures address the controls in the AU family.

title: Event Logging
control_text: Identify event types for logging; coordinate logging function; specify event types for logging; provide rationale; review and update event types.
discussion: An event is an observable occurrence in a system relevant to security and privacy.
enhancements: AU-02(01): Compilation of audit records from multiple sources.

title: Content of Audit Records
control_text: Ensure audit records contain: what type of event; when it occurred; where it occurred; source; outcome; identity of associated individuals or entities.
discussion: Audit record content includes event descriptions timestamps source and destination addresses user identifiers and success/fail indications.
enhancements: AU-03(01): Additional audit information; AU-03(03): Limit PII elements.

title: Audit Log Storage Capacity
control_text: Allocate audit log storage capacity to accommodate retention requirements.
discussion: Organizations consider types of audit logging and processing requirements when allocating storage capacity.

title: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
control_text: Alert personnel in event of audit logging process failure; take additional actions as defined.
discussion: Audit logging process failures include software and hardware errors and reaching storage capacity.
enhancements: AU-05(01)-AU-05(02): Storage capacity warning; real-time alerts.

title: Audit Record Review Analysis and Reporting
control_text: Review and analyze audit records for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity; report findings; adjust review level based on risk changes.
discussion: Audit record review analysis and reporting covers information security and privacy related logging.
enhancements: AU-06(01)-AU-06(06): Automated process integration; correlate repositories; integrated analysis.

title: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
control_text: Provide audit record reduction and report generation capability supporting on-demand review and after-the-fact investigations.
discussion: Audit record reduction organizes collected audit log information into a summary format.

title: Time Stamps
control_text: Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps; record time stamps meeting defined granularity using UTC or local time with offset.
discussion: Time stamps generated by the system include date and time commonly expressed in UTC.
enhancements: AU-08(01): Synchronization with authoritative time source.

title: Protection of Audit Information
control_text: Protect audit information and tools from unauthorized access modification and deletion; alert upon detection of unauthorized access.
discussion: Audit information includes all information needed to successfully audit system activity.
enhancements: AU-09(02)-AU-09(04): Separate physical systems; access by subset of privileged users.

title: Audit Record Retention
control_text: Retain audit records for defined time period to support investigations and meet retention requirements.
discussion: Organizations retain audit records until determined no longer needed for operational purposes.

title: Audit Record Generation
control_text: Provide audit record generation capability for defined event types; allow personnel to select event types; generate records including defined content.
discussion: Audit records can be generated from many different system components.
enhancements: AU-12(01)-AU-12(03): System-wide audit trail; changes by authorized individuals.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate assessment authorization and monitoring policy and procedures.
discussion: Assessment authorization and monitoring policy and procedures address the controls in the CA family.

title: Control Assessments
control_text: Select appropriate assessor; develop control assessment plan; ensure plan is approved; assess controls to determine effectiveness; produce assessment report.
discussion: Organizations assess controls in systems and environments as part of the system development life cycle.
enhancements: CA-02(01)-CA-02(03): Independent assessors; specialized assessments; leveraging external results.

title: Information Exchange
control_text: Approve and manage information exchange between systems using appropriate agreements; document interface characteristics and requirements; review and update.
discussion: System connections are authorized by senior agency officials or designees.
enhancements: CA-03(06)-CA-03(07): Transfer authorizations; transitive information exchanges.

title: Plan of Action and Milestones
control_text: Develop plan of action and milestones to document planned remediation actions; update based on assessment findings and monitoring activities.
discussion: Plans of action and milestones are useful for planning implementing and documenting remediation actions.

title: Authorization
control_text: Assign authorizing official for system and common controls; ensure authorization before commencing operations; update authorizations periodically.
discussion: Authorizations are official management decisions to authorize operation of systems.

title: Continuous Monitoring
control_text: Develop and implement continuous monitoring strategy including metrics frequencies ongoing assessments correlation analysis response actions and reporting.
discussion: Continuous monitoring at system level facilitates ongoing awareness of security and privacy posture.

title: Internal System Connections
control_text: Authorize internal connections; document interface characteristics and requirements; terminate connections after defined conditions; review continued need.
discussion: Organizations allow internal connections only after verifying security and privacy requirements can be satisfied.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate configuration management policy and procedures.
discussion: Configuration management policy and procedures address the controls in the CM family.

title: Baseline Configuration
control_text: Develop document and maintain current baseline configuration under configuration control; review and update periodically and when components are installed.
discussion: Baseline configurations include connectivity operational and communications aspects of systems.
enhancements: CM-02(02)-CM-02(07): Automation support; retention of previous configurations; high-risk areas.

title: Configuration Change Control
control_text: Determine and document configuration-controlled changes; review and approve changes; document decisions; implement approved changes; retain records; monitor activities.
discussion: Configuration change control involves systematic proposal justification implementation testing review and disposition.
enhancements: CM-03(01)-CM-03(06): Automated documentation; testing and validation; security representatives; cryptography.

title: Impact Analyses
control_text: Analyze changes to the system to determine potential security and privacy impacts prior to change implementation.
discussion: Organizational personnel with security or privacy responsibilities conduct impact analyses.
enhancements: CM-04(01)-CM-04(02): Separate test environments; verification of controls.

title: Access Restrictions for Change
control_text: Define document approve and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to the system.
discussion: Changes to hardware software or firmware can potentially have significant effects on security.
enhancements: CM-05(01): Automated access enforcement and audit records.

title: Configuration Settings
control_text: Establish and document configuration settings reflecting most restrictive mode; implement settings; identify and approve deviations; monitor and control changes.
discussion: Configuration settings are parameters that can be changed in hardware software or firmware components.
enhancements: CM-06(01)-CM-06(02): Automated management; respond to unauthorized changes.

title: Least Functionality
control_text: Configure system to provide only mission essential capabilities; prohibit or restrict use of specified functions ports protocols and services.
discussion: Systems provide a wide variety of functions and services some of which may not be necessary.
enhancements: CM-07(01)-CM-07(05): Periodic review; prevent program execution; authorized software.

title: System Component Inventory
control_text: Develop and document inventory of system components that accurately reflects the system; review and update periodically.
discussion: System components are discrete identifiable information technology assets.
enhancements: CM-08(01)-CM-08(04): Updates during installation; automated maintenance; unauthorized component detection.

title: Configuration Management Plan
control_text: Develop document and implement configuration management plan addressing roles responsibilities processes and procedures.
discussion: Configuration management activities occur throughout the system development life cycle.

title: Software Usage Restrictions
control_text: Use software in accordance with contract agreements and copyright laws; track software protected by quantity licenses; control peer-to-peer file sharing.
discussion: Software license tracking can be accomplished by manual or automated methods.

title: User-Installed Software
control_text: Establish policies governing user software installation; enforce policies through defined methods; monitor compliance.
discussion: If provided necessary privileges users can install software in organizational systems.
enhancements: CM-11(02): Software installation with privileged status.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate contingency planning policy and procedures.
discussion: Contingency planning policy and procedures address the controls in the CP family.

title: Contingency Plan
control_text: Develop contingency plan identifying essential functions recovery objectives roles and responsibilities; distribute review update and communicate plan changes.
discussion: Contingency planning for systems is part of an overall program for achieving continuity of operations.
enhancements: CP-02(01)-CP-02(08): Coordinate with related plans; capacity planning; resume and continue functions.

title: Contingency Training
control_text: Provide contingency training consistent with assigned roles; review and update training content periodically.
discussion: Contingency training is linked to assigned roles and responsibilities of organizational personnel.

title: Contingency Plan Testing
control_text: Test contingency plan periodically using defined tests; review test results; initiate corrective actions.
discussion: Methods for testing include checklists walk-through and tabletop exercises and simulations.
enhancements: CP-04(01)-CP-04(02): Coordinate with related plans; alternate processing site.

title: Alternate Storage Site
control_text: Establish alternate storage site with necessary agreements; ensure equivalent controls.
discussion: Alternate storage sites are geographically distinct from primary storage sites.
enhancements: CP-06(01)-CP-06(03): Separation from primary site; accessibility.

title: Alternate Processing Site
control_text: Establish alternate processing site for transfer and resumption of operations; make equipment available; provide equivalent controls.
discussion: Alternate processing sites are geographically distinct from primary processing sites.
enhancements: CP-07(01)-CP-07(04): Separation; accessibility; priority of service; preparation for use.

title: Telecommunications Services
control_text: Establish alternate telecommunications services for resumption of operations when primary capabilities unavailable.
discussion: Telecommunications services are needed to transmit information between systems.
enhancements: CP-08(01)-CP-08(02): Priority of service; single points of failure.

title: System Backup
control_text: Conduct backups of user-level system-level and documentation information at defined frequencies; protect backup confidentiality integrity and availability.
discussion: System-level information includes system state operating system software middleware and application software.
enhancements: CP-09(01)-CP-09(08): Testing for reliability; test restoration; transfer to alternate site; cryptographic protection.

title: System Recovery and Reconstitution
control_text: Provide for recovery and reconstitution of system to known state within defined time period after disruption compromise or failure.
discussion: Recovery is executing contingency plan activities to restore organizational mission and business functions.
enhancements: CP-10(02)-CP-10(04): Transaction recovery; restore within time period.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate identification and authentication policy and procedures.
discussion: Identification and authentication policy and procedures address the controls in the IA family.

title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
control_text: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.
discussion: Organizations can satisfy requirements by complying with HSPD 12.
enhancements: IA-02(01)-IA-02(12): Multi-factor authentication to privileged and non-privileged accounts; separate device; replay resistant.

title: Device Identification and Authentication
control_text: Uniquely identify and authenticate defined devices before establishing local remote or network connection.
discussion: Devices requiring unique identification and authentication are defined by type device or combination.

title: Identifier Management
control_text: Manage system identifiers: receive authorization; select identifier; assign to intended entity; prevent reuse; manage by disabling after inactivity.
discussion: Common device identifiers include MAC addresses IP addresses or device-unique token identifiers.

title: Authenticator Management
control_text: Manage authenticators: verify identity for initial distribution; establish initial content; ensure sufficient strength; establish administrative procedures; change defaults; refresh periodically; protect from unauthorized disclosure; require specific controls.
discussion: Authenticators include passwords cryptographic devices biometrics certificates one-time password devices and ID badges.
enhancements: IA-05(01)-IA-05(13): Password-based; public key-based; protection; no embedded static authenticators; federated credential management.

title: Authentication Feedback
control_text: Obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect from exploitation.
discussion: Authentication feedback from systems does not provide information that would allow unauthorized compromise.

title: Cryptographic Module Authentication
control_text: Implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet applicable requirements.
discussion: Authentication mechanisms may be required within a cryptographic module to authenticate an operator.

title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users)
control_text: Uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users or processes acting on their behalf.
discussion: Non-organizational users include system users other than organizational users explicitly covered by IA-02.
enhancements: IA-08(01)-IA-08(04): Acceptance of PIV credentials; external authenticators; defined profiles.

title: Re-authentication
control_text: Require users to re-authenticate when defined circumstances or situations require it.
discussion: Organizations may require re-authentication in certain situations beyond device locks.

title: Identity Proofing
control_text: Identity proof users requiring accounts based on appropriate identity assurance level; resolve to unique individual; collect validate and verify evidence.
discussion: Identity proofing is the process of collecting validating and verifying a claimed identity.
enhancements: IA-12(02)-IA-12(06): Identity evidence; validation and verification; in-person; address confirmation.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate incident response policy and procedures.
discussion: Incident response policy and procedures address the controls in the IR family.

title: Incident Response Training
control_text: Provide incident response training consistent with assigned roles; review and update training content periodically.
discussion: Incident response training is associated with assigned roles and responsibilities.
enhancements: IR-02(01)-IR-02(02): Simulated events; automated training environments.

title: Incident Handling
control_text: Implement incident handling capability including preparation detection analysis containment eradication and recovery; coordinate with contingency planning; incorporate lessons learned.
discussion: Organizations recognize that incident response capabilities depend on system capabilities.
enhancements: IR-04(01)-IR-04(11): Automated processes; information correlation; automatic disabling; external coordination.

title: Incident Monitoring
control_text: Track and document incidents on an ongoing basis.
discussion: Documenting incidents includes maintaining records about each incident and status.
enhancements: IR-05(01): Automated tracking data collection and analysis.

title: Incident Reporting
control_text: Require personnel to report suspected incidents within defined time period; report incident information to defined authorities.
discussion: Types of incidents reported reflect applicable laws and regulations.
enhancements: IR-06(01)-IR-06(03): Automated reporting; supply chain coordination.

title: Incident Response Assistance
control_text: Provide incident response support resource offering advice and assistance for handling and reporting incidents.
discussion: Incident response support resources include help desks assistance groups and automated ticketing systems.
enhancements: IR-07(01): Automation support for availability of information.

title: Incident Response Plan
control_text: Develop incident response plan providing roadmap for implementation; describe structure and organization; define reportable incidents and metrics; distribute and update plan.
discussion: It is important that organizations develop and implement a coordinated approach to incident response.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate maintenance policy and procedures.
discussion: Maintenance policy and procedures address the controls in the MA family.

title: Controlled Maintenance
control_text: Schedule document and review maintenance records; approve and monitor all maintenance activities; require approval for off-site removal; sanitize equipment; verify controls after maintenance.
discussion: Controlling system maintenance addresses information security aspects of the maintenance program.

title: Nonlocal Maintenance
control_text: Approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance; allow use of nonlocal tools consistent with policy; employ strong authentication; maintain records; terminate sessions when completed.
discussion: Nonlocal maintenance is conducted by individuals communicating through external or internal networks.
enhancements: MA-04(01)-MA-04(03): Logging and review; comparable security and sanitization.

title: Maintenance Personnel
control_text: Establish process for maintenance personnel authorization; verify non-escorted personnel possess required authorizations; designate personnel to supervise.
discussion: Maintenance personnel refers to individuals who perform hardware or software maintenance.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate media protection policy and procedures.
discussion: Media protection policy and procedures address the controls in the MP family.

title: Media Access
control_text: Restrict access to defined types of digital and non-digital media to defined personnel or roles.
discussion: System media includes digital and non-digital media including flash drives and magnetic tapes.

title: Media Sanitization
control_text: Sanitize system media prior to disposal release or reuse using defined techniques; employ mechanisms commensurate with security category.
discussion: Media sanitization applies to all digital and non-digital system media subject to disposal or reuse.

title: Media Use
control_text: Restrict or prohibit use of defined types of system media; prohibit portable storage devices with no identifiable owner.
discussion: System media includes both digital and non-digital media.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate physical and environmental protection policy and procedures.
discussion: Physical and environmental protection policy and procedures address the controls in the PE family.

title: Physical Access Authorizations
control_text: Develop approve and maintain list of individuals with authorized facility access; issue credentials; review access list periodically; remove individuals when access no longer required.
discussion: Authorization credentials include ID badges identification cards and smart cards.

title: Physical Access Control
control_text: Enforce physical access authorizations at entry and exit points; maintain access audit logs; control publicly accessible areas; escort visitors; secure keys and combinations.
discussion: Physical access control applies to employees and visitors.

title: Monitoring Physical Access
control_text: Monitor physical access to detect and respond to physical security incidents; review access logs; coordinate with incident response.
discussion: Physical access monitoring includes publicly accessible areas within organizational facilities.
enhancements: PE-06(01): Intrusion alarms and surveillance equipment.

title: Visitor Access Records
control_text: Maintain visitor access records for defined time period; review records periodically; report anomalies.
discussion: Visitor access records include names organizations signatures identification dates and purposes.

title: Emergency Shutoff
control_text: Provide capability of shutting off power in emergency situations; place switches in accessible locations; protect from unauthorized activation.
discussion: Emergency power shutoff primarily applies to facilities with concentrations of system resources.

title: Emergency Power
control_text: Provide uninterruptible power supply to facilitate orderly shutdown or transition to alternate power.
discussion: Short-term uninterruptible power supplies are primarily intended to provide time for orderly shutdown.

title: Emergency Lighting
control_text: Employ and maintain automatic emergency lighting that activates in event of power outage or disruption.
discussion: Emergency lighting covers interior and exterior areas within the facility.

title: Fire Protection
control_text: Employ and maintain fire detection and suppression systems that are supported by an independent energy source.
discussion: Fire detection and suppression systems reduce the risk of fire-related damage to organizational facilities.
enhancements: PE-13(01)-PE-13(03): Detection systems; suppression systems; automatic notification.

title: Environmental Controls
control_text: Maintain temperature and humidity levels within facility; monitor environmental controls at defined frequency.
discussion: Environmental controls apply to all areas within organizational facilities.
enhancements: PE-14(01)-PE-14(02): Automatic controls; monitoring with alarms.

title: Water Damage Protection
control_text: Protect the system from damage resulting from water leakage by providing master shutoff or isolation valves.
discussion: The provision of water damage protection primarily applies to organizational facilities.

title: Delivery and Removal
control_text: Authorize control and manage the entry and exit of defined system components; maintain records of system components.
discussion: Enforcing authorizations for entry and exit of system components may require restricting access to delivery areas.

title: Alternate Work Site
control_text: Determine and document alternate work sites; employ controls at alternate sites; assess effectiveness of controls.
discussion: Alternate work sites include government facilities or private residences of employees.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate planning policy and procedures.
discussion: Planning policy and procedures address the controls in the PL family.

title: System Security and Privacy Plans
control_text: Develop security and privacy plans that define authorization boundary; describe operational context; identify individuals in defined roles; describe control implementation; are reviewed and approved.
discussion: System security and privacy plans are scoped to the system and system components.
enhancements: PL-02(03): Plan and coordinate with other organizational entities.

title: Rules of Behavior
control_text: Establish and provide to individuals requiring access rules describing responsibilities and expected behavior; receive signed acknowledgment before authorizing access.
discussion: Rules of behavior represent an agreement between the user and the organization.
enhancements: PL-04(01): Social media and external site/application usage restrictions.

title: Baseline Selection
control_text: Select a control baseline for the system.
discussion: Control baselines provide a starting point for the control selection process.

title: Baseline Tailoring
control_text: Tailor the selected control baseline by applying specified tailoring actions.
discussion: The tailoring process includes identifying common controls and applying scoping considerations.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate personnel security policy and procedures.
discussion: Personnel security policy and procedures address the controls in the PS family.

title: Position Risk Designation
control_text: Assign a risk designation to all organizational positions; establish screening criteria for individuals filling those positions; review and update designations.
discussion: Position risk designations reflect Office of Personnel Management policy and guidance.

title: Personnel Screening
control_text: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to the system; rescreen individuals per defined conditions.
discussion: Personnel screening and rescreening activities reflect applicable laws and regulations.
enhancements: PS-03(03): Information requiring special protective measures.

title: Personnel Termination
control_text: Upon termination of individual employment: disable system access within defined time period; terminate authenticators and credentials; conduct exit interviews; retrieve security-related property; retain access to information and systems formerly controlled by terminated individual.
discussion: Timely execution of termination actions is essential for individuals who have been terminated for cause.

title: Personnel Transfer
control_text: Review and confirm ongoing operational need for current access authorizations when individuals are reassigned or transferred; initiate defined actions within defined time period; modify access authorization as needed.
discussion: Personnel transfer applies when reassignments or transfers are permanent.

title: Access Agreements
control_text: Develop and document access agreements for organizational systems; review and update agreements periodically; ensure individuals have signed before being granted access.
discussion: Access agreements include nondisclosure agreements acceptable use agreements rules of behavior and conflict-of-interest agreements.

title: External Personnel Security
control_text: Establish personnel security requirements for external provider personnel; require providers to comply with policies and procedures; document personnel security requirements; monitor provider compliance.
discussion: External provider personnel include service bureau contractors and other organizations providing system development and maintenance.

title: Personnel Sanctions
control_text: Employ a formal sanctions process for individuals failing to comply with established security and privacy policies and procedures; notify defined personnel when a formal sanctions process is initiated.
discussion: The sanctions process is consistent with applicable laws and regulations.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate risk assessment policy and procedures.
discussion: Risk assessment policy and procedures address the controls in the RA family.

title: Security Categorization
control_text: Categorize the system and information processed stored and transmitted; document the security categorization results in the security plan.
discussion: Security categories describe the potential adverse impacts to organizational operations and assets.

title: Risk Assessment
control_text: Conduct a risk assessment to identify threats vulnerabilities and risk to organizational operations assets individuals and other organizations; document risk assessment results; review and update periodically.
discussion: Risk assessments consider threats vulnerabilities likelihood and impact to organizational operations.

title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
control_text: Monitor and scan for vulnerabilities in the system and hosted applications at defined frequency; employ vulnerability monitoring tools; analyze vulnerability scan reports; remediate legitimate vulnerabilities; share information from vulnerability monitoring.
discussion: Security categorization of information and systems guides the frequency and comprehensiveness of vulnerability monitoring.
enhancements: RA-05(02)-RA-05(11): Update vulnerabilities; breadth and depth of coverage; privileged access; automated trend analyses.

title: Risk Response
control_text: Respond to findings from security and privacy assessments monitoring and audits in accordance with organizational risk tolerance.
discussion: Organizations have many options for responding to risk including accepting avoiding mitigating sharing and transferring.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate system and services acquisition policy and procedures.
discussion: System and services acquisition policy and procedures address the controls in the SA family.

title: Allocation of Resources
control_text: Determine the high-level information security and privacy requirements for the system; determine plan and document the resources required; include resources in capital planning.
discussion: Resource allocation includes funding for system security and privacy.

title: System Development Life Cycle
control_text: Acquire develop and manage the system using a system development life cycle that incorporates information security and privacy considerations.
discussion: A well-defined system development life cycle provides the foundation for the successful development implementation and operation.

title: Acquisition Process
control_text: Include security and privacy functional requirements in the acquisition contract; required design and development processes; required testing and evaluation procedures; required documentation.
discussion: The acquisition process documents include solicitation documents and contracts.
enhancements: SA-04(01)-SA-04(10): Functional properties; design and implementation; development methods; dynamic code analysis.

title: System Documentation
control_text: Obtain or develop administrator documentation and user documentation for the system; document attempts to obtain unavailable documentation; protect documentation.
discussion: Administrator documentation includes documentation of configurable parameters.

title: Security and Privacy Engineering Principles
control_text: Apply systems security and privacy engineering principles in the specification design development implementation and modification of the system.
discussion: Systems security and privacy engineering principles are closely related to and can be viewed as a generalization of security and privacy design principles.

title: External System Services
control_text: Require that providers of external system services comply with organizational security and privacy requirements; define and document oversight and user roles; employ defined processes to monitor compliance.
discussion: External system services are provided by an external provider and the organization has no direct control.
enhancements: SA-09(02): Identification of functions ports protocols and services.

title: Developer Configuration Management
control_text: Require the developer of the system to perform configuration management during development implementation and operation; document approve and control changes; track security flaws.
discussion: Organizations consider the quality and completeness of configuration management activities.

title: Developer Testing and Evaluation
control_text: Require the developer to create and implement a security and privacy assessment plan; perform testing and evaluation at defined depth and coverage; produce evidence of execution; correct flaws.
discussion: Developmental testing and evaluation confirms that required controls are implemented correctly.
enhancements: SA-11(01)-SA-11(08): Static code analysis; threat modeling; dynamic code analysis; manual code reviews.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate system and communications protection policy and procedures.
discussion: System and communications protection policy and procedures address the controls in the SC family.

title: Denial-of-Service Protection
control_text: (a) [Selection: Protect against; Limit] the effects of the following types of denial-of-service events: [organization-defined types]; and (b) Employ [organization-defined controls by type of denial-of-service event] to achieve the denial-of-service objective.
discussion: Denial-of-service events may occur due to a variety of internal and external causes.

title: Boundary Protection
control_text: (a) Monitor and control communications at the external managed interfaces to the system and at key internal managed interfaces within the system; (b) Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal organizational networks; and (c) Connect to external networks or systems only through managed interfaces.
discussion: Managed interfaces include gateways routers firewalls guards and encrypted tunnels.
enhancements: SC-07(03)-SC-07(29): Access points; external telecommunications services; deny by default; split tunneling; route traffic to proxy.

title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
control_text: Protect the [Selection (one or more): confidentiality; integrity] of transmitted information.
discussion: Protecting the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information applies to internal and external communications.
enhancements: SC-08(01): Cryptographic protection; SC-08(02): Pre- and post-transmission handling.

title: Network Disconnect
control_text: Terminate the network connection associated with a communications session at the end of the session or after a defined time period of inactivity.
discussion: Network disconnect applies to internal and external networks.

title: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
control_text: Establish and manage cryptographic keys when cryptography is employed within the system in accordance with [organization-defined requirements for key generation, distribution, storage, access, and destruction].
discussion: Cryptographic key management and establishment can be performed using manual procedures or automated mechanisms.

title: Cryptographic Protection
control_text: (a) Determine the [organization-defined cryptographic uses]; and (b) Implement the following types of cryptography required for each specified cryptographic use: [organization-defined types of cryptography for each specified cryptographic use].
discussion: Cryptography can be employed to support many security solutions.

title: Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications
control_text: (a) Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and applications with the following exceptions: [organization-defined exceptions]; and (b) Provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.
discussion: Collaborative computing devices and applications include remote meeting devices and applications networked white boards cameras and microphones.

title: Public Key Infrastructure Certificates
control_text: Issue public key certificates under an appropriate certificate policy or obtain public key certificates from an approved service provider.
discussion: Public key infrastructure certificates are certificates with visibility external to organizational systems.

title: Mobile Code
control_text: (a) Define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies; and (b) Authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system.
discussion: Mobile code technologies include Java JavaScript ActiveX Postscript PDF Flash and VBScript.

title: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Authoritative Source)
control_text: (a) Provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries; and (b) Provide the means to indicate the security status of child zones and enable verification of a chain of trust.
discussion: Providing authoritative source information enables external clients to obtain origin authentication and integrity verification.

title: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)
control_text: Request and perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the name/address resolution responses the system receives from authoritative sources.
discussion: Each client of name resolution services either performs this validation on its own or has authenticated channels to trusted validation providers.

title: Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service
control_text: Ensure the systems that collectively provide name/address resolution service for an organization are fault-tolerant and implement internal/external role separation.
discussion: Systems that provide name/address resolution services include DNS servers.

title: Session Authenticity
control_text: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.
discussion: Protecting session authenticity addresses communications protection at the session level.

title: Protection of Information at Rest
control_text: Protect the [Selection (one or more): confidentiality; integrity] of the following information at rest: [organization-defined information at rest].
discussion: Information at rest refers to the state of information when it is not in process or in transit.

title: Process Isolation
control_text: Maintain a separate execution domain for each executing system process.
discussion: Systems can maintain separate execution domains for each executing process by assigning each process a separate address space.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate system and information integrity policy and procedures.
discussion: System and information integrity policy and procedures address the controls in the SI family.

title: Flaw Remediation
control_text: (a) Identify, report, and correct system flaws; (b) Test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation; (c) Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within [organization-defined time period] of the release of the updates; and (d) Incorporate flaw remediation into the organizational configuration management process.
discussion: The need to remediate system flaws applies to all types of software and firmware.
enhancements: SI-02(02): Automated flaw remediation status; SI-02(03): Time to remediate flaws and benchmarks for corrective actions.

title: Malicious Code Protection
control_text: (a) Implement [Selection (one or more): signature-based; non-signature-based] malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code; (b) Automatically update malicious code protection mechanisms as new releases are available; (c) Configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform periodic scans and real-time scans; and (d) Address the receipt of false positives and resulting potential impact.
discussion: System entry and exit points include firewalls remote-access servers workstations electronic mail servers web servers proxy servers and notebook computers.
enhancements: SI-03(01)-SI-03(10): Central management; automatic updates; non-privileged users.

title: System Monitoring
control_text: (a) Monitor the system to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks and unauthorized connections; (b) Identify unauthorized use of the system through monitoring techniques and methods; (c) Invoke internal monitoring capabilities or deploy monitoring devices strategically; (d) Analyze detected events and anomalies; (e) Adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk; (f) Obtain legal opinion regarding system monitoring activities; and (g) Provide system monitoring information to defined personnel or roles.
discussion: System monitoring includes external and internal monitoring.
enhancements: SI-04(01)-SI-04(25): System-wide intrusion detection; automated tools; inbound and outbound communications traffic; wireless intrusion detection.

title: Security Alerts Advisories and Directives
control_text: (a) Receive system security alerts, advisories, and directives from [organization-defined external organizations] on an ongoing basis; (b) Generate internal security alerts, advisories, and directives as deemed necessary; (c) Disseminate security alerts, advisories, and directives to defined personnel; and (d) Implement security directives in accordance with established time frames.
discussion: Security alerts and advisories provide important information about security issues.

title: Information Input Validation
control_text: Check the validity of the following information inputs: [organization-defined information inputs to the system].
discussion: Checking the valid syntax and semantics of system inputs is important for correct operation of the system.

title: Error Handling
control_text: (a) Generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited; and (b) Reveal error messages only to [organization-defined personnel or roles].
discussion: Organizations consider the structure and content of error messages.

title: Information Management and Retention
control_text: Manage and retain information within the system and information output from the system in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, guidelines, and operational requirements.
discussion: Information management and retention requirements cover the full life cycle of information.

title: Memory Protection
control_text: Implement the following controls to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution: [organization-defined controls].
discussion: Some adversaries launch attacks with the intent of executing code in non-executable regions of memory or in memory locations that are prohibited.

title: Policy and Procedures
control_text: Develop document and disseminate supply chain risk management policy and procedures.
discussion: Supply chain risk management policy and procedures address the controls in the SR family.

title: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan
control_text: (a) Develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research and development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations and maintenance, and disposal of [organization-defined systems, system components, or system services]; (b) Review and update the supply chain risk management plan [organization-defined frequency].
discussion: Supply chain risk management plans address risks associated with the global and distributed nature of product and service supply chains.

title: Supply Chain Controls and Processes
control_text: (a) Establish a process or processes to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes; (b) Employ [organization-defined supply chain controls] to protect against supply chain risks; and (c) Document the selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls.
discussion: Supply chain elements include organizations entities or tools employed for the research and development design manufacturing acquisition delivery integration and maintenance of systems.

title: Acquisition Strategies Plans and Processes
control_text: Employ acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks.
discussion: The use of acquisition and procurement processes by organizations early in the system development life cycle provides an important vehicle to protect the supply chain.

title: Supplier Assessments and Reviews
control_text: Assess and review the supply chain-related risks associated with suppliers or contractors and the system, system component, or system service they provide [organization-defined frequency].
discussion: An assessment and review of supplier risk includes security and supply chain risk management processes.

title: Notification Agreements
control_text: Establish agreements and procedures with entities involved in the supply chain for the system for notification of supply chain compromises and results of assessments or audits.
discussion: The establishment of agreements and procedures facilitates communications among supply chain entities.

title: Inspection of Systems or Components
control_text: Inspect [organization-defined systems or system components] [Selection (one or more): at random; at [organization-defined frequency]; upon [organization-defined indications of need for inspection]] to detect tampering.
discussion: The inspection of systems or system components for tampering addresses both physical and logical tampering.

title: Component Authenticity
control_text: (a) Develop and implement anti-counterfeit policy and procedures that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system; and (b) Report counterfeit system components to [organization-defined external reporting organizations].
discussion: Sources of counterfeit components include manufacturers distributors and vendors in the supply chain.
enhancements: SR-11(01)-SR-11(02): Anti-counterfeit training; configuration control for component service and repair.

title: Component Disposal
control_text: Dispose of [organization-defined data, documentation, tools, or system components] using the following techniques and methods: [organization-defined techniques and methods].
discussion: Data documentation tools or system components can be disposed of at any time during the system development life cycle.
